dod_intent_evidence: U.S. Air Force SBIR Phase I recipient, preparing flight hardware for test under Air Force-supported work — channel notes.
score_evidence: "Multiple Engineering Positions" is the only job title in the pack, too generic to show a clear research-vs-field skew -> hiring_profile_skew
4-5 person team on a Phase I SBIR (the shortest, riskiest stage before Phase II eligibility), "preparing flight hardware for test" -> stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Autonomous ground/drone tracking products are described purely by capability ('autonomous target detection and tracking') with no mention of how tracks/alerts get relayed when the tactical network is degraded or intermittent.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The same DDIL failure mode as the canonical crowd-detection case: an autonomous tracker that assumes a continuous link back to command breaks the moment comms go intermittent, unless it's architected for on-device inference and store-and-forward from day one.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: A 4-person team at Phase I is focused on getting the sensor and tracking algorithm working at all, not yet on the tactical-network integration layer.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Ground Systems: Deployable custom sensor suites and ground mobility platforms including integrated processing, AI systems, and autonomous target detection and tracking capabilities.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The product catalog references 'security requirements' affecting lead times but never names ITAR, export control, or CMMC explicitly, despite selling flight hardware and biometric facility-access/security systems — both controlled-technology categories.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 4-person company without a named ITAR/CMMC compliance path risks exactly the paperwork-kills-the-program failure mode Barry targets, especially once flight hardware and facility biometric systems move past prototype.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Compliance infrastructure is typically the last thing a 4-person engineering-led team builds while still proving the hardware works.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Lead times vary by supply chain conditions and security requirements.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Operator readiness' is mentioned once, in the context of simulation/synthetic test environments, with no elaboration on who trains the actual field operator or how sustainment (spares, repair, GFE integration) works once hardware is fielded.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Simulation-based operator readiness is not the same as field sustainment — a jammed optical tracker or dead battery at an austere site needs a named person and spares pipeline, which is exactly the gap this language papers over.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's public materials stop at 'rapid validation,' i.e. pre-deployment testing, and don't yet extend to post-fielding sustainment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Scenario-based modeling and synthetic test environments for rapid validation and operator readiness.

opener_hook: Your Phase I flight hardware is heading to test — is CMMC/ITAR compliance already lined up for the Phase II transition, or still ahead of you?
what_they_do: Builds electro-optical sensor payloads, ground/space tracking systems, and facility-security sensors for defense and space customers, currently under an Air Force SBIR Phase I preparing flight hardware for test.
